reviews.review_text: Moving into Avana Tempe was a terrible experience right from the beginning. Attempting to work with the office to move in was extremely frustrating - everything from getting answers to my questions about paperwork they sent me, actually obtaining needed documents, and even paying the move in fees was difficult as the staff either does not want to help or does not have the proper training to do so. The leasing manager at the time, Michael, was especially difficult to work with during my move in. Upon move in, the apartment was in terrible condition, practically uninhabitable. It was so bad, that I actually went right back to the office after seeing the apartment to ask if it was ready for move in. I was really surprised at the terrible condition, especially since my original move in date was pushed back by Avana Tempe and I had to pay for an extra month at my previous apartment. When I was finally able to move in, the apartment was extremely dirty. My new home had dirt, stains, black marks and grease splatters on the walls and floors all throughout, but the worst part was what appeared to be large stains from leaking on the living room ceiling. When I spoke to Carol at the office, she stated that the cleaning crew had been in and she did offer to send them back. I declined because if the cleaners had already been and they thought the condition of the apartment was acceptable, they would not do a better job if they came a second time so I had to clean the apartment myself. I was later told that maintenance came and looked at the leaking and stains on the ceiling, but I was not there when they entered, no notice of entry was left and nothing was done to improve the appearance or fix the issue at all so I am unsure if anyone even looked at this. I was also told that there was no mold, but I am also not sure if that is accurate. During my 7 months (March - October) at Avana Tempe, I submitted several maintenance requests, none of which were ever fully resolved in a timely manner and some of which were never resolved at all. - I submitted two requests for my kitchen light to be fixed as it would not turn on unless I flipped the switch up and down for several minutes or if I flipped the switch and left it on, it would come on hours later. Maintenance did come out on the first request, because I received a notice of entry, but whatever fix they implemented lasted about a week and then the same issue began again. I had to submit a second request before it was actually fixed. I was only made aware that maintenance had been in my home due to the light being fixed - no notice of entry was left. - I submitted one request for my garbage disposal as it just stopped working altogether. Maintenance came out and again, whatever they did lasted a couple of weeks and then it completely stopped working again. I did not submit a second request due to the fact that I was moving out. - My biggest concern was the Air Conditioning. I submitted at least four maintenance requests to have my AC looked at as it would turn on but was not blowing cold air and did not cool my home at all. I came home to an oven every day over the course of an Arizona summer, I had to buy my own fan and run it constantly but was unable to sleep in my own home due to it being so hot. I went into the office and spoke with the assistant manager, Danielle, who at the time, was extremely nice and I truly believed she would help get the issue fixed. At no time did maintenance enter my home to look at the AC while I was there, nor was any notice of entry ever left to indicate that the issue was being looked at or worked on. The issue was never resolved by Avana Tempe, and was only resolved due to the weather changing. - None of the above issues include the many notices from Avana Tempe about the AC, water and even the electricity being out for the entire complex. I had to move out early due to an out-of-state job relocation. I went into the office and spoke to the assistant manager, Danielle about this on 09.26.19 and was advised that I needed to pay a buy out fee and provide 60 days notice. At no time did I become rude or disrespectful during this conversation. I did ask if Greystar would work with me since moving was completely out of my control and if the lease was terminated prior to 60 days, it would benefit both myself and Greystar because they had been renovating all the apartments. If I vacated earlier, they would be able to renovate sooner and in turn, begin charging a new tenant a much higher rent. Danielle said she would ask Tiffany(who I think was Danielle 's boss; I 'm not sure as no introductions were completed). I do not think Danielle or Tiffany understood what I was asking them and Tiffany was disengaged and aloof during the brief conversation. Danielle then provided me a piece of paper and told me to sign it, which I did. I was advised that I would be emailed a copy of the document that I had just signed and I thought the issue was resolved. Over the course of the next 60 days, I paid my rent online and on time, as I always had. I expected the online balance to reflect the buy out fee that I was verbally advised of and to calculate the prorated rent for my last month, but it did not show the fee and it showed a balance for the entire last month, not just the 1st - 26th. I paid the entire balance for the last month so that I would not be late and then I contacted the office to obtain a breakdown of the charges so that I could determine how much I had overpaid, and confirm the remainder of the fee so that I could pay it. I emailed the assistant manager directly since she was the one I had spoken to and when I did not receive a reply, I emailed again and CCed the general mailbox for the office, hoping that someone would be able to assist me. Danielle then sent me an unprofessional response in which she accused me of "refusing "to sign a second document that I was unaware of, and threatening that I would be in breech of the lease if I turned in my keys. Danielle also failed to provide the breakdown of charges that I requested so I was unable to verify the remaining amount owed. I responded to Danielle requesting that she discontinue treating me so poorly when all I was attempting to do was resolve the issue and complete my move out. I explained to her that I was unaware of the second document and I also let her know that I would be posting this review due to the many issues I had experienced during my stay, especially the fact that Avana Tempe "refused "to fix my Air Conditioning over the course of an Arizona summer. (I believe this is an ACTUAL breech of their lease, Section 30.) I never received a reply to this email, however days later I was emailed a Notice of Entry from a law office. Due to my inability to obtain a confirmation of the charges owed, I finally had to figure out the remaining amount due on my own by taking the second document that had not been provided to me until 11.12.19 and subtracting everything I had already paid. I then paid the difference via the online portal on 11.18.19 (within 7 days as stated by this document) and I then sent my own breakdown on the signed document to the office. The only response back was a Statement of Charges due, which was exactly what I overpaid for my last month 's rent, which was EXTREMELY frustrating because it was clear that not only was the office stonewalling me, but they were not even looking at my many attempts to resolve the situation as I had clearly outlined the overpayment in my email to them. I 'm very surprised that a company makes it so difficult to work with and pay them; I had trouble paying fees upon move in and then I struggled immensely trying to pay fees when I moved out. Also, because Danielle and Tiffany either did not understand what I was asking them about the 60 day notice, I called Greystar directly on several occasions so I could hopefully speak with someone who could help me and understand what I was asking. No one ever picked up the phone or returned my many voicemails in regard to this issue. I contacted Greystar directly again when I was unable to obtain a breakdown of the charges from the office - I emailed them on their website begging for someone to assist me, and received an almost immediate response, but it simply asked what community I was inquiring about. I responded and told them I was trying to work with Avana Tempe and I requested that they help me instead of simply forwarding my email to the community since the office staff had been treating me poorly and refusing to provide the requested information I needed to complete move out. I never received a response to this email, however I received a call from Spring Stewart the exact same day that i provided my own breakdown to the office. She left a voicemail stating that I could call her back, but she did not leave a number or extension to reach her. I called the generic number back and emailed, leaving messages requesting that she call back and she never did. Lastly, during my entire 7 months living at Avana Tempe, they were re-paining all of the buildings, re-surfacing all of the all of the pavement in the parking area, completing apartment renovations and completing an entire office renovation so I dealt with constant noise and outside messes, the pool and hot tub was closed the entire time, and then there was the additional inconvenience of not being able to use the main entry into the complex and not being able to park in my space for days. Due to the overall attitude of the office staff, the condition of the apartments, and the abhorrent way that I was treated when circumstances out of my control arose, I would not recommend renting from Avana Tempe. I would even go so far to discourage anyone from renting from any of the Greystar properties due to their complete lack of response when I reached out when the office staff refused to help me.

reviews.review_text: Dear Avana Management, I 've officially put my foot in my mouth. I had no idea that I could logically fit my size 10 shoe completely down my throat with such ease.... While things wear out and break down, it might seem simple to file a maintenance request and hope for the best, however, in the past (prior to 2024) it felt as though said requests were part of a larger project of trying to keep up a 40+ year old complex, and unfortunately, communication regarding requests was minimal probably because there were several repair projects taking place at any given moment. Still, I cannot imagine how difficult it is to keep up with all the requests and complaints you might receive. A week or so ago, I sent a letter to management regarding some work orders that had not been addressed in the past. Most of these work orders were concerning small issues in my unit, however, a few of these work orders were larger issues related to the property as a whole. In my haste, I neglected to consider the difficulty it might require for many of these work orders to be completed. A few days after I sent my letter to management, To my great surprise, every single item I was concerned about in my original set of work orders has been either addressed, or completely resolved. My sincerest apologies if anybody was effected by original letter I sent to management, I stand in complete awe at this sort of positive response. Just, WOW - Simply amazing. Additionally, The maintenance team member that you sent to fix everything was extremely polite, knowledgeable, and truthful about everything that had to be repaired. Staff was trusting and careful around my apartment as though they were working on their own home while conscious of personal items and cleanliness throughout the repair. All in all, I 'm completely surprised by this response, and as a result, I apologize to everybody for my previous letter. Thank you for diligence and urgency. My apartment is AWESOME!!!
